content.help: How visible HUD parts stay after a few quiet seconds. They light up fully when something changes and in combat.

Add dark text shadows for brighter backgrounds. Off keeps the original appearance. Subtle adds a light outline; Strong adds a heavier outline and shadow. Does not change text size, HUD layout or hide rules.

Makes all HUD text bigger or smaller: labels, names, tracker, subtitles, messages and the loot list. The small captions under the vital rings stop growing at 130% so the row stays clear of the compass. Large numbers (ammo count, quest titles) keep their size.
Makes the compass markers bigger or smaller: quests, doors, locations, waypoints, enemies, companions and mines. Icons grow upward so they never cover the compass ticks.

Makes the round icons bigger or smaller: the vital rings (health, AP, rads, weight, food, water, rest, armor), the active effect rings and the companion portraits. If the vitals row would reach the compass, food, water and rest move up to their own row.
Show your player level and XP progress row, including its perk reminder and karma readout. Turning this off hides the row; XP still updates and level-up banners keep their own setting.
Off hides Phosphor's crosshair everywhere, including third-person aiming. The game's own crosshair stays hidden.
Show hit and kill markers independently of the crosshair. Normal menu and power-armor visibility rules still apply.

content.text: Hide crosshair while aiming in third person
content.help: Off: keep the crosshair visible while aiming in third person. On: hide it while aiming, matching the previous behavior. First-person sights, scopes, menus and power armor keep their existing rules. Iron sights Show/Hide everything overrides this setting.
Choose 12-hour time with AM/PM (1:30 PM) or 24-hour military time (13:30).

content.text: Hide full health/AP and zero radiation
content.help: Off: always show the health, AP and radiation wheels. On: hide health when healed to its radiation-reduced maximum, AP when recovered to its fatigue-reduced maximum, and radiation at zero. Each wheel works independently from the survival-needs setting.
On: show the armor wheel (Warzone Armor Plates System). Off: hide it. The armor value keeps tracking either way, and the wheel only appears while that mod is installed.

content.text: Show location name only on arrival
content.help: Off: always show the location name. On: show it for 8 seconds on entering a different named location or loading a save, then fade it out. The countdown waits while paused or the location group is hidden. The clock and region stay unchanged.
On: nearby places you haven't discovered yet show on the compass as hollow, grey markers. Off: only discovered places show, like the vanilla Pip-Boy map.
Some mods use long-lasting items for permanent statuses. Effects longer than this stay off the effects tray. 0 shows everything.

Auto uses the Character Type you picked in Condition Boy, so Phosphor matches it. Vault Boy and Vault Girl need the figures folder made from Condition Boy's files; without it Phosphor falls back to its silhouette.
The figure appears as soon as a limb takes damage and stays lit while a limb is crippled.
Draw equipped armor pieces over the figure, like Condition Boy.

content.text: Phosphor shows, dims or hides each part of the HUD depending on what's on screen. Recommended uses Phosphor's rules; the other two override them for that situation.

content.help: Default: crosshair hidden, quests, companions and feed dimmed.
Default: only ammo, effects, stealth and the enemy bar stay up; compass and vitals dim.
Default: vitals (including AP), effects and ammo stay up; the rest hides.

Default: companions, feed and quest banners stay up so you see reactions; the game's own dialogue subtitles show in place of Phosphor's, positioned by the dialogue menu (for example Extended Dialogue Interface). Show everything uses Phosphor's subtitles instead.
Default: crosshair hidden, most of the HUD dimmed.
Default: feed, quest banners and subtitles stay up; the compass hides under the build bar.
Default: the vanilla power armor HUD takes over; Phosphor keeps only quests, companions and active effects.
Default: everything hides during NAF and AAF scenes.

content.text: Choose what stays on screen when you're not fighting. Parts come back when something changes, when health is low, or when you fire.

content.help: Wait this long after combat ends before applying these rules. Combat restores parts immediately.
Outside combat: Show keeps normal idle opacity, Dim uses 30% context opacity, and Hide removes this part until it wakes. Higher-priority situations keep their normal rules.
Outside combat: Show keeps normal idle opacity, Dim uses 30% context opacity, and Hide removes this part until it wakes. Higher-priority situations keep their normal rules.
Outside combat: Show keeps normal idle opacity, Dim uses 30% context opacity, and Hide removes this part until it wakes. Higher-priority situations keep their normal rules.
Outside combat: Show keeps normal idle opacity, Dim uses 30% context opacity, and Hide removes this part until it wakes. Higher-priority situations keep their normal rules.
Outside combat: Show keeps normal idle opacity, Dim uses 30% context opacity, and Hide removes this part until it wakes. Higher-priority situations keep their normal rules.
Outside combat: Show keeps normal idle opacity, Dim uses 30% context opacity, and Hide removes this part until it wakes. Higher-priority situations keep their normal rules.
Outside combat: Show keeps normal idle opacity, Dim uses 30% context opacity, and Hide removes this part until it wakes. Higher-priority situations keep their normal rules.
Near the limit shows the weight circle from 85% of your max; it turns red past 100%.
Survival only. Ten segments above your weapon, one per rank, with progress toward the next rank.
Shows Peckish, Parched, Tired and so on under the food, water and rest circles instead of percentages.
Off: always show food, water and rest in survival. On: show each circle only from Peckish, Parched or Tired onward, and hide it again once that need is satisfied.
Off matches vanilla survival, which hides enemies from the compass.

Markers over armed mines counting down at you, chevrons around the crosshair for ones you can't see, and the closest mine's distance and fuse. Replaces Mine Detector HUD's markers, so turn that mod off to avoid doubles.
Adds a marker on the compass for each armed mine.

content.text: Perk mods such as Alternative Activation Prompts, Scrap As You Go and You Are Exceptional add choices (scrap, harvest, equip, take all) that replace the quick-loot box with a choice wheel on containers and bodies. Pick a key below: the quick-loot box comes first, and holding the key brings the choices back.

content.help: On: on containers and dead bodies the quick-loot box shows, and perk activation choices wait until you hold the perk-choices key. Nothing changes until you pick a key. Off: the game's usual behavior. Other targets (people, robots that are alive, doors, items) are never affected. OG only for now: the AE edition ignores this section.

Hold this key while looking at a container or body to show perk activation choices instead of the quick-loot box. No key is set by default. If Dynamic Activation Key is installed, holding its key works too.
Shows your KARMA alignment beside your level, with your karma title when it changes. Turn off KARMA's own notifications and Vault-Boy pop-ups to avoid doubles.
Shows your REPUTATION title with the town or faction you're in, next to the location name.
Challenges you track in the CHALLENGES Pip-Boy tab show under the quest tracker with their progress.
Immersive Legendary Mutations hides the mutation message on purpose. Enemy bar only marks the mutation on the targeted enemy's bar; the feed option also posts a line.
A gold star on the compass where a legendary item dropped, until you pick it up.
Show the equipped weapon's legendary effects above the ammo counter. Off hides that line; the weapon name and ammo stay.
The big level number with your new perk and skill points. With it off, level-ups still post to the feed and the XP bar still rolls over.
Keeps a small perk (and LevelUpMenuEx skill) point count next to your level until you spend them.
